title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is from the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, in a combinatorial model of a stratified one-dimensional space (a 'line' L).
- Cells. L is a totally ordered finite set of vertices a < b < c < ... . The cells of M are the points P_a and the open segments S_ab (a < b). M_0 is the set of 0-cells.
- Order. X < Y ('pos', positionally) means X lies entirely to the left of Y.
- Incidence. |o| is a separation or disjointness relation between cells and sets of cells.
- Supports. For a set of cells Φ, supp°(Φ), also written s-pr°(Φ), is its support. cos-pr°(Φ) is the set of cells separated from Φ.

Top of page: end of the proof begun on the previous page. The claim being proved is: if Z < X then Z ∈ s-pr°(Φ). Take Z' with Z' |o| Φ; we must show Z |o| Z'. Write δX = {a, b}, so X = P_a or X = S_ab.
- Already handled on the previous page: Z' = P_a, and Z' < P_a.
- Remaining case: P_a < Z'. Since Z < X, we have Z ≤ P_a (Z is left of, or equal to, the left endpoint of X). Hence Z < Z', so Z and Z' are disjoint, i.e. Z |o| Z'. QED.

NB. Grothendieck remarks that he did not need the standing hypothesis 'Hyp.', and crossed out 'nor the constructibility of Φ'. He used only some property of Φ, Ψ; the word is illegible.

Proof of (b). It goes by induction on card δΦ, using part 1° together with a 'lemma of composition of segments'. For a < b < c and Φ = {S_ab, P_b, S_bc}, one has supp°(Φ) = supp°(S_ac). Topologically this is (a,b) ∪ {b} ∪ (b,c) = (a,c).

Proof of the lemma: it suffices that Φ and S_ac have the same complement. This follows from a slightly sharper statement. For X ∈ M:
- X lies left of Φ (i.e. X < S_ab) iff X < S_ac;
- X lies right of Φ (i.e. X > S_bc) iff X > S_ac.
Both are trivial and need no hypothesis.

Purpose. These steps belong to a theorem on the next page: the support of a constructible set Φ equals that of a 'non-crossing' Φ' obtained by resolving crossings. It is part of a combinatorial or tame description of constructible sets in a stratified space.
errors: No mathematical error. The step 'Z < X ⇒ Z ≤ P_a' tacitly uses that a is the left endpoint of X (a = b if X = P_a, a < b if X = S_ab); this holds by the setup on the previous page.
The phrase in the NB about what was actually used is illegible, so the exact hypothesis invoked cannot be confirmed.

ideas.what: Case analysis showing a cell strictly left of X is separated from any cell disjoint from Φ (support stability).
ideas.modern_name: elementary order-theoretic argument on cell complexes of a line / interval subdivision

ideas.what: Lemma of composition of segments: S_ab ∪ P_b ∪ S_bc has the same support as S_ac, proved by comparing left and right complements.
ideas.modern_name: refinement/subdivision invariance of supports in a cell decomposition of R (cf. cell decomposition in o-minimal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; o-minimal cell decomposition: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame-topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; this specific lemma unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: The page finishes a routine case analysis and proves the trivial fact that subdividing an open interval at an interior point does not change its support. It documents Grothendieck's combinatorial approach to tame topology in 1986, but contains nothing new or unexpected.
transcription_corrections: Subscript under ≤ and ≥ should read 'pos' (positionally), not 'pas'.
'(par card δΦ)' is written above 'récurrence de 1°' as an overbrace annotation: induction on card δΦ.
Line 2: 'Z ≤ P_a ou [struck]' — the crossed-out word is illegible (possibly 'Z = P_a' or similar); then 'donc on aura Z < Z′'.
NB line: 'que Φ / Ψ [?] tend[?] dans pr[?]' is not legible; 'tend' is doubtful, and the phrase seems to describe a property of Φ, Ψ ('… des pr[…]').
